payload.hypothesis: Adding strictly-prior history aggregates as bucketized categorical fields (user prior long_view rate + prior count, user×tab prior rate, video prior long_view rate) raises validation primary by at least +0.003 over the 5-field FM, because they supply dense, well-supported backoff crosses that the sparse user_id×video_id embedding cannot estimate.
payload.mechanism: GAUC and nDCG@5 only respond to within-user score variation. Two of the four new fields (video prior long_view rate, user x tab prior rate) vary across a user's own impressions and therefore move the ranking directly and first-order; the two user-level fields (rate bucket, count bucket) are constant within a user and contribute only through their pairwise FM terms with item/context fields - which is precisely the useful part, because they partition users into propensity strata whose embeddings are estimated from thousands of rows instead of the handful of rows behind a single user_id. That gives the model a smoothed backoff for the 98% of validation pairs whose exact user-video cross is untrained, and gives the item-side field a time-varying popularity estimate that a static video_id embedding cannot express.
payload.predicted: +0.003 to +0.006 valid primary (0.6045-0.6075); anything below +0.002 is inside the noise floor and the change is reverted
payload.invalid_if: Validation primary lands within +/-0.002 of 0.60147, or the no-history bucket dominates (i.e. coverage of the user-rate field is far below the 98% C13 predicts), or a per-field ablation shows the whole delta is carried by the video-side rate alone (which would make it a restatement of item popularity, already worth only 0.5807 standalone).
evidence: C13: 98.1% of validation users have >=1 prior train interaction (median 35, mean 47), but only 1.62% of validation rows have a prior interaction on the same video and 3.38% on the same author - fine-grained pair history is unusable, user-level history is nearly universal.

C12: only 1.627% of validation user-video pairs were ever seen in train, so the FM's user_id x video_id interaction is essentially untrained for 98% of the rows it must rank; a coarse user-propensity stratum x video cross has orders of magnitude more support.

C15: removing `tab` costs -0.0159 primary, ~8x epsilon - scenario context is the single strongest non-identity field, so a user x tab prior affinity is aggregating over the axis that already carries the most signal.

C2: purely user-side first-order terms are exactly zero for this metric, so these fields must (and do, in an FM) act through interactions with video_id / author_id / tab / dur_bucket, plus the item-side prior rate which varies within a user's list directly.

Journal: iters 1 and 2 refuted loss-side changes (listwise -0.00318, BPR hybrid -0.00337) on the *existing* representation; the representation itself has never been given behavioral history at all (organizer headroom idea 2, untested here).
Section 0b of the rules ships harness.history.prior_stats with proven guarantees: strictly-earlier only, ties are not predecessors, and test outcomes never enter any aggregate.
payload.reason: Delta is -0.00191, roughly 4 sigma below the noise floor and clearly negative rather than the predicted +0.003 to +0.006. Both GAUC and nDCG@5 dropped versus parent (0.6674->0.6650, 0.5357->0.5341), so the history buckets are not helping the item-side ranking or the user-conditioned cross terms; the invalid_if condition ('lands within +/-0.002... reverted') is met on the negative side, which is stronger than the stated null.
payload.mechanism_update: Bucketized prior-rate/count fields added as extra categorical fields expand the FM's field count and add first-order + pairwise noise terms without clearly improving estimability. Either the smoothing/prior_weight=20 or the coarse quantile bucketing destroys the fine-grained signal that raw user_id/video_id embeddings already capture reasonably well from context+id crosses, or the extra 5 fields dilute the model's limited capacity/interactions (consistent with C5's finding that adding more static/derived categorical fields to this exact FM tends to slightly hurt rather than help). The theorized backoff-for-sparse-crosses mechanism does not survive contact with the pairwise FM structure at this scale.
deprioritise: adding coarse bucketized history aggregates as raw categorical fields to the 5-field FM
further expansion of field count / static feature stuffing on this exact FM formulation
